lesson.title: React useEffect() Hook Introduction
lesson.goal: learn the React useEffect hook: run side effects on mount and on state changes, and clean them up

goalMatch.note: This video covers exactly what you asked for: useEffect on mount (empty array), on state changes (dependencies), and cleanup via the return function.

steps.title: Set up counter component
steps.instructions: Scaffold a Vite React project with `npm create vite@latest my-react-app -- --template react`, create `src/MyComponent.jsx` with a `count` state (useState(0)) and an Add button, render it in `src/App.jsx`, and run `npm run dev`. Import both `useState` and `useEffect` from react.

targets.caption: Import both useState and useEffect hooks from react

explanations.topic: What useEffect does and its three trigger modes
Common useEffect use cases and mounting vs unmounting

hints: Make sure you import both hooks inside curly braces from "react".
Use `const [count, setCount] = useState(0);` and an updater function `c => c + 1` inside `addCount`.

Return a fragment containing `

Count: {count}

` and ``.
common_mistakes: Calling `addCount()` immediately in `onClick={addCount()}` instead of passing the function reference `onClick={addCount}`.
steps.code:
import React, {useState, useEffect} from "react"; function MyComponent() { const [count, setCount] = useState(0); function addCount(){ setCount(c => c + 1); } return (<>

Count: {count}

); } export default MyComponent;

steps.title: Run useEffect on every render
steps.instructions: In `src/MyComponent.jsx`, call `useEffect` with an arrow function and no dependency array. Inside it, set `document.title` to a template string showing `Count: ${count}`.

targets.caption: Update the browser tab title inside useEffect

explanations.topic: Passing only a callback runs the effect after every re-render
Why an empty dependency array runs the effect only on mount

hints: Where should hooks be placed inside a React function component?
Place `useEffect(() => { ... });` near the top of `MyComponent` after `useState`.
Set `document.title = `Count: ${count}`;` using backticks inside the callback.
common_mistakes: Using single or double quotes instead of backticks for the `${count}` template literal.
Calling `useEffect` conditionally or inside another function like `addCount`.

steps.title: Restrict useEffect to mount only
steps.instructions: In src/MyComponent.jsx, pass an empty array `[]` as the second argument to `useEffect`. Save and click Add in the browser to confirm the title updates once on mount only.

targets.caption: Add an empty dependency array as the second argument

hints: What second argument tells `useEffect` not to re-run after mount?
Add a comma after the closing brace of the arrow function and pass `[]`.
Your hook call should end with `}, []);`.
common_mistakes: Omitting the comma between the callback function and the dependency array.
Passing `[]` inside the callback body instead of as the second argument to `useEffect`.

steps.title: Trigger useEffect when count changes
steps.instructions: In src/MyComponent.jsx, pass [count] as the dependency array to useEffect so it runs on mount and whenever count changes. Add a subtractCount function and a Subtract button to confirm the title updates on both increments and decrements.

targets.caption: Add count to the dependency array

explanations.topic: How a dependency value differs from omitting the dependency array

hints: Which state variable should React watch to re-run the title update?
Put `count` inside the dependency array `[count]`.
Duplicate `addCount` as `subtractCount` using `setCount(c => c - 1);` and wire it to a Subtract button.
common_mistakes: Putting `"count"` as a string in the dependency array instead of the `count` variable.
Forgetting to include the `<button onClick={subtractCount}>Subtract</button>` element in JSX.
steps.code: useEffect(() => { document.title = `Count: ${count}`; }, [count]); function subtractCount(){ setCount(c => c - 1); }

steps.title: Track multiple dependencies in useEffect
steps.instructions:
In src/MyComponent.jsx, add a color state starting at "green", a changeColor button that toggles it between green and red, and style the

with the color. Include color in document.title and in the dependency array [count, color].

targets.caption: Include both count and color in the dependency array
Bind inline paragraph color to state

explanations.topic: What happens when color is used inside the effect but omitted from dependencies
Benefits of useEffect for code organization and controlling re-runs

hints: Notice what happens if `color` is in `document.title` without being in the dependency array.
Use a ternary operator inside `setColor(c => c === "green" ? "red" : "green")`.
Update the dependency array to `[count, color]` so either change updates the title.
common_mistakes: Using single curly braces `style={color: color}` instead of double curly braces `style={{color: color}}` for a JSX style object.
Forgetting to add `color` to `[count, color]`, causing stale title values when clicking Change Color.
steps.code: const [color, setColor] = useState("green"); useEffect(() => { document.title = `Count: ${count} ${color}`; }, [count, color]); function changeColor(){ setColor(c => c === "green" ? "red" : "green"); }

steps.title: Attach resize listener on mount
steps.instructions:
In src/MyComponent.jsx, add `width` and `height` states initialized from `window.innerWidth` and `window.innerHeight`, render both in `

` tags, and define `handleResize` to update them. Call `window.addEventListener("resize", handleResize)` inside a `useEffect` with an empty dependency array so it runs only on mount.

targets.caption: Attach resize listener inside mount-only useEffect

explanations.topic: Why adding event listeners outside useEffect attaches thousands of duplicates
Why React Strict Mode runs setup and cleanup twice in development

hints: Why shouldn't `window.addEventListener` sit directly in the component body?
Wrap `window.addEventListener("resize", handleResize);` inside `useEffect(() => { ... }, []);`.

Display `

Window Width: {width}px

` and `

Window Height: {height}px

` in the returned JSX.
common_mistakes: Omitting the `[]` dependency array, which registers a new resize listener on every window resize re-render.
Calling `handleResize()` in `addEventListener("resize", handleResize())` instead of passing the function reference.
steps.code: const [width, setWidth] = useState(window.innerWidth); const [height, setHeight] = useState(window.innerHeight); useEffect(() => { window.addEventListener("resize", handleResize); console.log("EVENT LISTENER ADDED"); }, []); function handleResize(){ setWidth(window.innerWidth); setHeight(window.innerHeight); }

steps.title: Return a useEffect cleanup function
steps.instructions: In src/MyComponent.jsx, return an arrow function from the resize `useEffect` that calls `window.removeEventListener("resize", handleResize)` and logs a cleanup message. Open the browser DevTools console to see the cleanup log.

targets.caption: Remove the event listener in the returned cleanup function

explanations.topic: When the cleanup function returned by useEffect runs
Using multiple useEffect hooks in a single component

hints: How do you tell `useEffect` to clean up resources when unmounting?
At the bottom of the `useEffect` callback, add `return () => { ... }`.
Inside the returned function, call `window.removeEventListener("resize", handleResize);`.
common_mistakes: Calling `window.removeEventListener` directly inside `useEffect` instead of inside a returned function.
Passing a different function or anonymous callback to `removeEventListener` instead of the exact `handleResize` reference.
steps.code: useEffect(() => { window.addEventListener("resize", handleResize); console.log("EVENT LISTENER ADDED"); return () => { window.removeEventListener("resize", handleResize); console.log("EVENT LISTENER REMOVED"); } }, []);

steps.title: Add a second useEffect hook
steps.instructions: In src/MyComponent.jsx, add a second `useEffect` that sets `document.title` to `Size: ${width} x ${height}`. Pass `[width, height]` as its dependency array so the tab title updates as you resize.

targets.caption: Update document.title inside a separate useEffect hook

hints: Can a React component contain more than one `useEffect` hook?
Add a second `useEffect(() => { ... }, [width, height]);` below the first hook.
Assign `document.title = `Size: ${width} x ${height}`;` inside the new effect.
common_mistakes: Nesting the second `useEffect` inside the first `useEffect` instead of keeping them as siblings.
Using `[]` instead of `[width, height]`, which prevents the document title from updating on resize.
